content.text: Six lamps are written into `parts/room-13.mjs`, but in the real build the room is still dark. The lock refuses every lamp because the mansion shell claims the hall's air. In a scratch copy with only that claim removed, the six lamps light the room (min 8, 0 dark, 0 dim). input.summary:
Upper hall lamp plan: six standing lanterns at y11 in parts/room-13.mjs build(g), placed after the furniture gate and clear of the designer's layout, supported and off the stair hole. Measured in a scratch copy with the shell's interior air claim removed: min 8, 0 dark, 0 dim, no fit flags from the lamps.
Real build.nbt is written, but the room is still dark (min 0, 57 dark, 41 dim): runParts refuses all six lamp writes because parts/shell.mjs box() (lines 26-27) fills the whole interior with WALL then carves air, so the shell claims every hall air cell.
Fix for the shell owner: fill only the perimeter walls, not the interior volume. Verified in scratch: shell placed 22734 -> 12484, no REFUSED lines in any part, lamps accepted.
left: Real build: the six lamp writes at (46,47), (49,47), (46,43), (49,43), (46,59), (49,52) y11 are refused by runParts ("lantern air" claimed by the mansion shell). The room is not lit until parts/shell.mjs box() stops claiming interior air. This is a shell change, so I did not make it.
Scratch copy /tmp/lamp-scratch-13 has the perimeter-only shell and is the evidence for the lamp plan; it is not part of the run and can be discarded.
Hallway to nowhere at (45,11,59): the south end of the hall is a 34-cell dead end with no door or cupboard (fit issue, designer's layout). A lamp does not fix it.

FURNISH is still false, so no furniture is built. The focal hall table at z60 and its lantern are absent, and the light was measured on the empty hall. The lamp cells avoid the designer's cells, so they stay clear if FURNISH is set true.
Cells over the grand stair's hole (x45..46, z54..57, no y10 floor) and its rail at x47 cannot take a lamp, so the south-west is lit from (46,59) only.

waste.tool: `mcd room --lamps` (or the LAMPS suggestion) should propose only cells that are free, unreserved by any designer layout, and have a solid top face under them; the current suggestions ignore support and the stair hole.

waste.what: Working out why the lamps were refused: I read shell.mjs by hand, then built a scratch copy to see the interior air claim.
waste.cost: about 4 extra builds and one scratch copy
waste.tool: runParts' refusal report should name the claiming part and the call (e.g. "claimed by mansion shell box() fill"), not just "earlier parts".

companions.task: Interior partitions and room walls: the shell's box() should lay only the perimeter walls, leaving the room volumes as air the room parts can own. The plasterer would take the shell's interior fill and confirm the partitions still close.
The south dead end of the upper hall (z58..60): a cupboard or door at the end, so the hall isn't a 34-cell hallway to nowhere, and the hall table focal piece when FURNISH is turned on.
